precepts.text: Remember the scripture says a spiritual man discerneth all things.
precepts.point: Now, let me say this now. Remember the scripture says a spiritual man discerneth all things. You can hear. Where's that one in Sirach? Divers meats. No, no, no. False speeches. Yeah. Yeah, that's it. A palate. That's it. I forgot it. Oh, Sirach 36. Hold this. We're going to come right back here. Sirach 36:19.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
Ananias and Sapphira sold a possession and “kept back part of the price”. It was their property anyway; they did not have to lie. But Peter said, “Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost, and to keep back part of the price of the land?”

Nobody had to tell Peter that. He already knew. That was the spirit of God working those senses. When he saw him, he already knew something was not right with this man, something was not right with this spirit: you are dealing evil right now. That is what the scripture means: “But he that is spiritual judgeth all things”. A spiritual man discerns all things.

Sirach shows how that discerning works: “As the palate tasteth divers kinds of venison: so doth an heart of understanding false speeches.” When you eat, you do not have to see; you can tell the difference between chicken and beef, chicken and fish, without looking. So a heart of understanding can discern false speech. One way: a man who is talking too much. You do not have to convince anyone of the truth.

Peter told him, “thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God.” And “Ananias hearing these words fell down, and gave up the ghost: and great fear came on all them that heard these things.” The fear came because Peter was able to discern lies and truth. We laugh about it because we know it is true: when you are not moving right and a brother in the spirit sees it, you wonder how he knew. That is clear knowing, the spiritual senses trained and at work.

precepts.text: Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins. A savior brings salvation, and that salvation is for the children of Israel. The slave masters taught that they and their slaves were equally capable of salvation; that is not how it goes.
precepts.point: They are the most needy of any people in our country, the book said. It does say needy, and the Bible says it too.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
In 1673 Mr. Baxter published his Christian Directory with directions to masters in foreign plantations who have negroes and other slaves, a rubric to follow. In their evil minds they really believed they were masters. Did the Lord allow this to happen? Absolutely. But that is not what Colossians 3:22 is talking about. The first direction: remember that they have immortal souls and are equally capable of salvation with yourselves. That is where the false sense of equality comes from. It comes from slavery; it comes from Christianity.

Who is salvation for? “Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins.” A savior brings salvation, and that salvation is only for the children of Israel.

They believed they could be saved and then us; they are the people, and we come after. That is not how it goes. The same directions said that they and you are equally under the government and laws of God, and that is incorrect: we are not equal with these people. Christ was exalted to give repentance to Israel, so the servants of Colossians and the salvation preached to them belong to Israel.

precepts.text: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the Most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty. This is the place; this is where you find your rest and your protection.
precepts.point: We have to learn to come back to the Lord and walk in righteousness, because that man does not know peace; all he knows is war. Even though he loves saying the word peace, like his president: I will be known as the most peaceful president ever.

note.label: I Come In Peace

precepts.why:
God exalted Christ “to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins.” Repentance is for Israel, the children of the captivity, of the slave trade, of the colonization of Africa, not the fake people in the land right now. The law was only given to us. Esau's only job is to whoop us into shape. We are in punishment right now; it is like we are in jail and they are the correction officers. We just have to do our time in peace and we are going to come out. But while we do our time, any time we move weirdly, they will break our back.

So when brothers say we should gather guns and go fight Esau: Negro, something is wrong with you. The Bible said the sword was his gift; the Lord gave him the sword. Read the name written on your gun: Smith & Wesson. We don't make guns; the AK-47 is the Russians, the Uzi is the Israelis. All they have to do is cut the water off in the hood. In Haiti a gang leader bought five of ten cases of bullets from a rich oligarch's man, and within the hour the police came, a three hour shootout used up all his bullets, and he had to call the same rich man for the rest. That is the setup: America will have a shootout with you, make you waste your bullets, and then you are dead. In 1985 they dropped a bomb on MOVE in Philly; at Waco, Esau came with tanks on white people, an offshoot of the Seventh-day Adventist Church, with kids inside. Stop playing.

Your only defense against this man is the Bible. “He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.” This is the place. This is where you find your rest and your protection.

We have to learn to come back to the Lord and walk in righteousness, because that man does not know peace. All he knows is war, even though he loves saying the word peace. The protection of Israel is not in the sword but in dwelling with the Most High, the same God who exalted Christ to give Israel repentance and forgiveness.

precepts.text: Why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost? Satan whispers thoughts and puts things in your head that are not there, even 'the deacon does not like you.' Every one of us gets attacked in the mind, the deacon included.
precepts.point: How do those evil things get into the mind? Acts shows it: Satan fills the heart.

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

precepts.why:
Christ said evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders and the rest come “from within, out of the heart of men”, and “defile the man.” So how do those evil things get into your mind? Remember who the war is against: Satan. Acts shows how he does it.

“But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession, And kept back part of the price, his wife also being privy to it, and brought a certain part, and laid it at the apostles' feet. But Peter said, Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost” What did Satan do? He filled his heart to lie. That lying spirit comes from Satan.

That is how he works. He is there in your head, whispering thoughts, tempting you, putting things there that are not there. The deacon says something to you and Satan says, why did he say that to you? The deacon don't like you. A husband gives his wife an order to clean the bathroom, and Satan whispers: you going to let him talk to you like that, after all you do in this house? He don't understand you; he don't love you. If she listens, she becomes bitter and it shows in her actions.

Satan puts things in everyone's head, the deacon included. The fight with Satan starts first and foremost in your mind, and many fall in this truth because they wait until the mind is already defiled. To win, you have to kill it right there: the thoughts Satan puts in your mind should never become action. Ask, why am I thinking like this? Fast and pray, Lord take these thoughts out of my mind, and answer him with the word of God, “the sword of the Spirit”, the weapon we fight with.

precepts.text: Gamaliel warned the council with examples: Theudas boasted himself to be somebody and four hundred joined him, and he was slain and all who obeyed him scattered; Judas of Galilee drew away much people, and he perished and all who obeyed him were dispersed.
precepts.point: Moses said if these men die the common death of all men, the Lord hath not sent me; but if the earth open her mouth and swallow them up, then ye shall understand that these men have provoked the Lord. The ground clave asunder, they and their houses and goods went down alive into the pit, all Israel fled at their cry, and fire from the Lord consumed the two hundred and fifty. These things were written for our learning about leaders.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
Korah, Dathan, Abiram and On “took men”, “two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown”. They were not nobodies; they had a name, and what they had was influence over the congregation. They used it against Moses and Aaron: “Ye take too much upon you”. And the results of those leaders: the earth “swallowed them up, and their houses, and all the men that appertained unto Korah, and all their goods”, and fire from the Lord “consumed the two hundred and fifty men that offered incense.” Everyone who followed them went down with them.

These things were written aforetime for our learning, and Acts 5 shows the same lesson. The apostles were brought before the council, and Gamaliel stood up and warned them: “Ye men of Israel, take heed to yourselves what ye intend to do as touching these men.” Then he gave examples.

“For before these days rose up Theudas, boasting himself to be somebody; to whom a number of men, about four hundred, joined themselves”. Four hundred men joined themselves to a man who came across as a leader, and he “was slain; and all, as many as obeyed him, were scattered, and brought to nought.” Then “rose up Judas of Galilee in the days of the taxing, and drew away much people after him: he also perished; and all, even as many as obeyed him, were dispersed.”

That is the pattern with false leaders: the leader perishes, and the ones that obeyed him perish and are scattered with him, just like the men that appertained unto Korah. “For the leaders of this people cause them to err; and they that are led of them are destroyed.” The leaders of the black community today, the Christian pastors, have our people living in hell, with drugs, gang violence, shootings on the block and adultery, and those that follow them are destroyed with them.

precepts.text: Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree.
precepts.point: Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree. Christ was lynched, hanged on a tree, under the same curse as his people.

note.label: False New Year: Doctrine Slayer - True Past Curses & Trauma

precepts.why:
Peter and the other apostles told our wicked elders, “We ought to obey God rather than men.” And then: “The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree.” Christ was lynched.

Why does Peter call it a tree? What is the cross made of? Wood. Hanging on the cross is hanging on a tree. He says it again in Acts 10:39: “whom they slew and hanged on a tree”. Some say he was hanged from an actual tree, but Thomas said, “Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe.” What would they need nails for on a tree? His hands and feet were nailed to a cross, and he hung there for hours, lynched slowly. And they mocked him: “If thou be the Son of God, come down from the cross.” A man hanging by the neck from a tree could not be answering questions; he would be choking to death. So Peter called the crucifixion hanging on a tree, and the two men beside him were lynched too.

It is ironic: the same way the white man lynched us in slavery and into the 60s is the same way our King was killed. That is why Galatians 3:13 matters: “Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree”. Christ was hanged on a tree under the same curse as his people.

precepts.text: Him hath God exalted to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins; Christ died for the nation of Israel.
precepts.point: The letters of Paul were written to Israelites living in those lands and called by their names, Romans and Corinthians, the same way we are called American or Jamaican today; written today they would be the letter to the Jamaicans or the letter to the Puerto Ricans.

note.label: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out

precepts.why:
“The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree. Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins.”

Christ died for the nation of Israel: repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins. That is the forgiveness the trespass offering gave, “it shall be forgiven him”, now given through the Prince and Saviour who is the offering without blemish and the atonement himself.

precepts.text: Refrain from these men and let them alone, for if this work be of men it will come to naught, but if it be of God you cannot overthrow it, lest you be found to fight against God.
precepts.point: When we keep the commandments, those who devise wickedness against us are going to get cast down, whether it be another nation or one of our own people. If you come against the work of the Most High, you are fighting against him, not against the man you see with your face.

note.label: Psalm 36: The Transgression of the Wicked

precepts.why:
“Let not the foot of pride come against me, and let not the hand of the wicked remove me. There are the workers of iniquity fallen: they are cast down, and shall not be able to rise.” Acts shows why they fall: “Refrain from these men, and let them alone: for if this counsel or this work be of men, it will come to nought: But if it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it; lest haply ye be found even to fight against God.”

When we keep the commandments, those who devise wickedness against us are going to get cast down, whether it be another nation or one of our own people. If you come against the work of the Most High, you are fighting against him, not against the man you see with your face, and you cannot overthrow it.

When we keep the commandments, like Deacon Yawasap says, the angels get activated, and when the angels get activated our enemies get the destruction coming to them, no matter how much they have.

precepts.text: Ananias and Sapphira kept back part of the price and lied to Peter, an example of covering transgression.
precepts.point: He that covers a transgression seeks love, but he that repeats a matter separates very friends. Covering sin like Ananias and Sapphira, who conspired to lie to the apostles, is condemned.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“He that covereth a transgression seeketh love; but he that repeateth a matter separateth very friends.” Covering a transgression is condemned. “But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession”, and they kept back part of the price and lied to Peter.

Ananias and Sapphira conspired to lie to the apostles. That is covering transgression, and it is the example of what Proverbs 17 condemns.

precepts.text: If this counsel be of men it will come to nought, but if it be of God it cannot be overthrown, lest men be found fighting against God.
precepts.point: If the counsel is from man it will fall, but if it is from the Most High it cannot be overthrown, and men would only end up fighting against God.

note.label: Isaiah 8: Maher-shalal-hash-baz, the Snare, and the Law and the Testimony

precepts.why:
“Take counsel together, and it shall come to nought; speak the word, and it shall not stand: for God is with us.” Gamaliel said the same of the apostles: “Refrain from these men, and let them alone: for if this counsel or this work be of men, it will come to nought: But if it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it; lest haply ye be found even to fight against God.”

If the counsel is from man it will fall, but if it is from the Most High it cannot be overthrown, and men would only end up fighting against God. So the people of far countries may associate themselves and gird themselves, but they shall be broken in pieces, because their counsel is of men and God is with us.

precepts.text: The Most High raised up Jesus and exalted him to be a Prince and a Saviour, to give repentance to Israel, naming the nation he died for.
precepts.point: Caiaphas prophesied that one man should die for the people, speaking not of himself but from the prophecies he knew in Isaiah 53 and the Psalms. That nation he must die for is Israel, and "not for that nation only" means Christ would also gather the children of God scattered abroad, the twelve tribes, not the Gentiles the Christians claim.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
Peter names the nation Christ died for: “The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree. Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins.”

A Prince and a Saviour to give repentance to Israel. That is the nation Caiaphas prophesied one man should die for.

precepts.text: None lacked, for possessors of lands and houses sold them and laid the price at the apostles' feet, distributed to every man as he had need.
precepts.point: Money is only a tool to further the people and the ministry; use wisdom and give only as much as you have, so you do not sell everything and end up begging the congregation.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
Ananias continues from the end of Acts 4: “Neither was there any among them that lacked: for as many as were possessors of lands or houses sold them, and brought the prices of the things that were sold, And laid them down at the apostles’ feet: and distribution was made unto every man according as he had need.”

None among the believers lacked. The church was the epicenter of the community, where counsel was given and economic and community problems were resolved, the way the black Wall Street towns like Rosewood and Tulsa once kept the dollar circulating among our own people for months before it left. That is the practice Ananias and Sapphira came into with part of the price.

precepts.text: Joses, surnamed Barnabas, a Levite of Cyprus, sold his land and brought the money and laid it at the apostles' feet.
precepts.point: Money is only a tool to further the people and the ministry; use wisdom and give only as much as you have, so you do not sell everything and end up begging the congregation.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
Right before Ananias comes the honest example: “And Joses, who by the apostles was surnamed Barnabas, (which is, being interpreted, The son of consolation,) a Levite, and of the country of Cyprus, Having land, sold it, and brought the money, and laid it at the apostles’ feet.”

Barnabas sold his land and laid the money down at the apostles' feet. Money is only a tool to further the people and the ministry. Use wisdom and give only as much as you have, so you do not sell everything and end up begging the congregation; but what you bring, bring honestly.

precepts.text: All that believed were together and had all things common, selling their possessions and parting to all men as they had need.
precepts.point: Money is only a tool to further the people and the ministry; use wisdom and give only as much as you have, so you do not sell everything and end up begging the congregation.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“And all that believed were together, and had all things common; And sold their possessions and goods, and parted them to all men, as every man had need.”

A community is a people with all things in common: common government, common heritage, common interest and common culture, and the word community itself comes from the root common. So-called black people today are not yet a community, divided by religion, politics and color, until they come into the fullness of Christ. What the believers had in Acts 2 is what Ananias was pretending to take part in.

precepts.text: Be renewed in the spirit of your mind, put on the new man, and put away lying, speaking truth, for we are members one of another.
precepts.point: Their word was their bond; they vowed a vow and were bound to pay it. A man's word shows his character, so if you cannot do a thing, be honest and say so rather than swear to what you cannot perform.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“And be renewed in the spirit of your mind; And that ye put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness. Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour: for we are members one of another.”

To be renewed in the spirit of the mind is to be born again, to reboot the mind and clear out the programming of this world's philosophy. The new man puts away lying and speaks truth with his neighbour, because we are members one of another. Ananias did not put away lying as the renewed mind requires; the spirit upon him was covetousness as well as lying, for they saw the full value and coveted it.

precepts.text: Grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption.
precepts.point: Their word was their bond; they vowed a vow and were bound to pay it. A man's word shows his character, so if you cannot do a thing, be honest and say so rather than swear to what you cannot perform.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“And grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption.”

Ananias lied to the Holy Ghost, and Peter tells him he has not lied unto men but unto God. Lying grieves the holy Spirit whereby we are sealed, which is why it is put away by the renewed mind.

precepts.text: Ye shall not steal, neither deal falsely, neither lie one to another.
precepts.point: Their word was their bond; they vowed a vow and were bound to pay it. A man's word shows his character, so if you cannot do a thing, be honest and say so rather than swear to what you cannot perform.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
The law is plain: “Ye shall not steal, neither deal falsely, neither lie one to another.”

Ananias dealt falsely and lied, keeping back part of the price while presenting it as the whole. While it remained it was his own, so the sin was not in keeping the land; it was in the lie and the covetousness behind it.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.
precepts.point: Their word was their bond; they vowed a vow and were bound to pay it. A man's word shows his character, so if you cannot do a thing, be honest and say so rather than swear to what you cannot perform.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.” It is one of the ten commandments.

Ananias bore false witness about the price of the land before the apostles, and Peter shows how far that reaches: he had not lied unto men but unto God.

precepts.text: When thou vowest a vow unto the Most High, slack not to pay it; that which is gone out of thy lips thou shalt keep.
precepts.point: Their word was their bond; they vowed a vow and were bound to pay it. A man's word shows his character, so if you cannot do a thing, be honest and say so rather than swear to what you cannot perform.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
Their word was their bond. “When thou shalt vow a vow unto the Lord thy God, thou shalt not slack to pay it: for the Lord thy God will surely require it of thee; and it would be sin in thee. But if thou shalt forbear to vow, it shall be no sin in thee.”

While the land remained it was his own, and after it was sold it was in his own power. He did not have to vow. But once he vowed, he was bound to pay it: “That which is gone out of thy lips thou shalt keep and perform; even a freewill offering, according as thou hast vowed unto the Lord thy God, which thou hast promised with thy mouth.” Ananias vowed the whole and paid part.

precepts.text: Swear not at all, but let your communication be yea, yea, nay, nay, for whatsoever is more cometh of evil.
precepts.point: Their word was their bond; they vowed a vow and were bound to pay it. A man's word shows his character, so if you cannot do a thing, be honest and say so rather than swear to what you cannot perform.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
Christ said, “Swear not at all”, not by heaven, not by the earth, not by Jerusalem, not by your head. “But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.”

A man's word shows his character. If you cannot do a thing, be honest and say so rather than swear to what you cannot perform. Ananias's yea was not yea, and what was more than that came of evil.

precepts.text: Shall we continue in sin that grace may abound? God forbid; how shall we that are dead to sin live any longer therein?
precepts.point: Grace covers the thorn you sincerely fight, not the sin you commit wilfully; there is a level of perfection the Most High looks for by generation, and not every man is given the same measure.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
This is after the death of Christ, under grace, and Ananias was put to death for lying and breaking his vow. “What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound? God forbid. How shall we, that are dead to sin, live any longer therein?”

Grace was never a licence to sin. Those who are dead to sin do not live any longer in it, and Ananias shows what happens under grace to the man who does.

precepts.text: The wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
precepts.point: Grace covers the thorn you sincerely fight, not the sin you commit wilfully; there is a level of perfection the Most High looks for by generation, and not every man is given the same measure.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.”

The wages of sin is death, even now, after Christ. Ananias earned those wages at the apostles' feet, and great fear came on all that heard it.

precepts.text: Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law, for sin is the transgression of the law.
precepts.point: Grace covers the thorn you sincerely fight, not the sin you commit wilfully; there is a level of perfection the Most High looks for by generation, and not every man is given the same measure.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.” Sin is defined by the law, so the law is still standing under grace.

The christian church hands out a licence to sin by teaching the law is done away and all is covered by grace. It is answerable for the blood in the community when men sin presumptuously believing there are no consequences. Ananias transgressed the law and paid its wages.

precepts.text: As sin hath reigned unto death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life.
precepts.point: Grace covers the thorn you sincerely fight, not the sin you commit wilfully; there is a level of perfection the Most High looks for by generation, and not every man is given the same measure.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“That as sin hath reigned unto death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.”

Grace reigns through righteousness, not apart from it. Sin still reigns unto death, as it did over Ananias; grace is for the man walking in righteousness.

precepts.text: It shall be our righteousness if we observe to do all these commandments before the Most High.
precepts.point: Grace covers the thorn you sincerely fight, not the sin you commit wilfully; there is a level of perfection the Most High looks for by generation, and not every man is given the same measure.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
What is the righteousness grace reigns through? “And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.”

Righteousness is observing to do the commandments. So grace through righteousness is grace through keeping the law, the opposite of the licence to sin the church hands out.

precepts.text: If we sin wilfully there remains no more sacrifice; he that despised Moses' law died without mercy under two or three witnesses, and sorer punishment awaits those who tread under foot the Son of God, for it is fearful to fall into the hands of the living God.
precepts.point: Grace covers the thorn you sincerely fight, not the sin you commit wilfully; there is a level of perfection the Most High looks for by generation, and not every man is given the same measure.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.”

Grace covers the thorn you sincerely fight, not the sin you commit wilfully. “He that despised Moses’ law died without mercy under two or three witnesses: Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God”. The punishment under Christ is sorer, not lighter.

There is a level of perfection the Most High looks for by generation, and not every man is given the same measure. “Vengeance belongeth unto me, I will recompense, saith the Lord. And again, The Lord shall judge his people. It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.” Ananias fell into those hands.

precepts.text: The Most High commanded no man to do wickedly, nor gave any man a licence to sin.
precepts.point: The witness under Christ is not two or three men but the Most High himself and the angels who always behold his face, so nothing is hidden from him.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“He hath commanded no man to do wickedly, neither hath he given any man licence to sin.”

Sapphira shared her husband's fate because they agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Most High. A wife submits to her husband as unto the Most High, in righteousness, not in wickedness; if he tells her to break the law, she is not to agree with him, because no man has been given licence to sin. A wife is meant to be a tower against death and a help meet. Had she refused the evil or brought it to the leadership, she could have saved his life, as Abigail did.

precepts.text: Their angels do always behold the face of my Father which is in heaven.
precepts.point: The witness under Christ is not two or three men but the Most High himself and the angels who always behold his face, so nothing is hidden from him.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“Take heed that ye despise not one of these little ones; for I say unto you, That in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father which is in heaven.”

The witness under Christ is not two or three men. It is the Most High himself and the angels who always behold his face. Ananias and Sapphira agreed together in private, but nothing is hidden from him.

precepts.text: The eyes of the Most High are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men.
precepts.point: The witness under Christ is not two or three men but the Most High himself and the angels who always behold his face, so nothing is hidden from him.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“Such a man only feareth the eyes of men, and knoweth not that the eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts.”

Sapphira feared the eyes of men and kept the story straight for them. But the eyes of the Most High behold all the ways of men and consider the most secret parts, and the agreement she made with her husband was not secret to him.

precepts.text: Unto every one of us is given grace according to the measure of the gift of Christ.
precepts.point: The witness under Christ is not two or three men but the Most High himself and the angels who always behold his face, so nothing is hidden from him.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“But unto every one of us is given grace according to the measure of the gift of Christ.”

Not everyone has the same measure of grace. One man is put to death for a smaller sin while David was spared far greater ones, for grace is given by the measure of the gift of Christ. Ananias and Sapphira were given their measure, and great fear came upon all the church.

precepts.text: These signs shall follow them that believe: casting out devils, speaking with new tongues, and laying hands on the sick that they recover.
precepts.point: In the last days the pattern is to call the elders of the church to pray over the sick and anoint with oil, for prophecies, tongues, and such knowledge would cease once the name of Christ was established.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
Christ had said, “And these signs shall follow them that believe; In my name shall they cast out devils; they shall speak with new tongues; They shall take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it shall not hurt them; they shall lay hands on the sick, and they shall recover.”

This is that fulfilled. They waited in Jerusalem for the Holy Ghost, the power was poured out, and now the sick are healed every one and the unclean spirits cast out, so that even the shadow of Peter passing by was sought.

precepts.text: Charity never faileth, but prophecies shall fail, tongues shall cease, and knowledge shall vanish away.
precepts.point: In the last days the pattern is to call the elders of the church to pray over the sick and anoint with oil, for prophecies, tongues, and such knowledge would cease once the name of Christ was established.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“Charity never faileth: but whether there be prophecies, they shall fail; whether there be tongues, they shall cease; whether there be knowledge, it shall vanish away.”

These gifts of healing and tongues were for that time, to introduce the Son of God and prove the power of the Most High on earth. Once the name of Christ was established, prophecies, tongues and such knowledge would cease. They are not the gifts of today, which is why our people still die of disease no matter what the pastors claim.

precepts.text: Is any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the church to pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord.
precepts.point: In the last days the pattern is to call the elders of the church to pray over the sick and anoint with oil, for prophecies, tongues, and such knowledge would cease once the name of Christ was established.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
The pattern for the last days: “Is any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord”.

Not the shadow of an apostle, not a healing line. The sick call for the elders of the church, who pray over him and anoint him with oil in the name of the Lord.

precepts.text: Confess your faults one to another and pray one for another; the effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.
precepts.point: In the last days the pattern is to call the elders of the church to pray over the sick and anoint with oil, for prophecies, tongues, and such knowledge would cease once the name of Christ was established.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.”

That is the healing given to us in the last days: confession, prayer one for another, and the fervent prayer of a righteous man, in place of the sign-gifts that were for the apostles' time.

precepts.text: A people who saw no signs would yet believe, showing the sign-gifts were not for today.
precepts.point: In the last days the pattern is to call the elders of the church to pray over the sick and anoint with oil, for prophecies, tongues, and such knowledge would cease once the name of Christ was established.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“Your houses will I give to a people that shall come; which not having heard of me yet shall believe me; to whom I have shewed no signs, yet they shall do that I have commanded them.”

A people who saw no signs would yet believe and do what he commanded. The sign-gifts were not for today; the multitudes healed in Solomon's porch were for that time, to prove the power of the Most High, and the people that shall come believe without them.

precepts.text: The word of the Lord came unto Jeremiah while he was yet shut up in the court of the prison.
precepts.point: Every man of the Most High went to prison, from Jeremiah, John, and Christ himself to Paul and Silas, as every man who fought oppression was jailed; the teacher who pushes prophecy is counted the same threat.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“Moreover the word of the Lord came unto Jeremiah the second time, while he was yet shut up in the court of the prison”. The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah in prison.

Every man of the Most High went to prison. Read the lives of the apostles and prophets as a pattern for today: the apostles put in the common prison here, Jeremiah shut up in the court of the prison before them. What the forefathers suffered will come again under America, the last kingdom, and worse.

precepts.text: When Jesus had heard that John was cast into prison, he departed into Galilee.
precepts.point: Every man of the Most High went to prison, from Jeremiah, John, and Christ himself to Paul and Silas, as every man who fought oppression was jailed; the teacher who pushes prophecy is counted the same threat.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“Now when Jesus had heard that John was cast into prison, he departed into Galilee”. John was cast into prison for the word he preached.

It is the same pattern: Jeremiah, John, and now the apostles in the common prison. If you teach this gospel, prison and loss will come, so you cannot be joined to this world.

precepts.text: A notable prisoner named Barabbas was set beside Jesus, who was delivered up and bound.
precepts.point: Every man of the Most High went to prison, from Jeremiah, John, and Christ himself to Paul and Silas, as every man who fought oppression was jailed; the teacher who pushes prophecy is counted the same threat.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

“And they had then a notable prisoner, called Barabbas.” Barabbas was set beside Jesus, who was delivered up and bound. Christ himself was in the hands of the authorities as a prisoner.

Every man who fought oppression was jailed, and a man who pushes prophecy is counted the same threat. Prepare for it: set aside a nest so your wife and family are provided for if you are locked up, for they will freeze accounts and take houses. The Most High will help, as he sent the angel to open the prison doors, but you must still prepare.

precepts.text: Paul and Silas were dragged before the magistrates, beaten with many stripes, and cast into prison.
precepts.point: Every man of the Most High went to prison, from Jeremiah, John, and Christ himself to Paul and Silas, as every man who fought oppression was jailed; the teacher who pushes prophecy is counted the same threat.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

Paul and Silas after the apostles: their accusers “caught Paul and Silas, and drew them into the marketplace unto the rulers, And brought them to the magistrates, saying, These men, being Jews, do exceedingly trouble our city, And teach customs, which are not lawful for us to receive, neither to observe, being Romans.”

“And when they had laid many stripes upon them, they cast them into prison, charging the jailor to keep them safely”. Beaten and jailed for teaching customs not lawful for the Romans.

From Jeremiah and John and Christ himself to Paul and Silas, every man of the Most High went to prison. What the forefathers suffered will come again under America, the last kingdom, and worse, so if you teach this gospel, you cannot be joined to this world.

precepts.text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom; a good understanding have all they that do his commandments.
precepts.point: The Holy Ghost is given only to them that obey the Most High; those who will not keep his commandments do not have it, however they claim it.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
Peter says the Holy Ghost is given to them that obey him. “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.”

A good understanding belongs to them that do his commandments. The Holy Ghost is given only to them that obey the Most High; those who will not keep his commandments do not have it, however they claim it.

precepts.text: Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you and make known my words unto you.
precepts.point: The Holy Ghost is given only to them that obey the Most High; those who will not keep his commandments do not have it, however they claim it.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you.”

Christ was exalted to give repentance to Israel, and the spirit is poured out on those who turn at his reproof. Christ came through the loins of David, from Judah, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; the law was given to Israel, so repentance from breaking the law is given to Israel. The apostles are his witnesses because their lineage experienced his ministry, death and miracles; popes and denominations are not witnesses. And the Holy Ghost comes to them that turn and obey.

precepts.text: The time cometh that whosoever killeth you will think that he doeth God service.
precepts.point: When men believe the law is done away they hold no morals to restrain them, and will put the teachers to death thinking they do the will of the Most High.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
Christ warned, “They shall put you out of the synagogues: yea, the time cometh, that whosoever killeth you will think that he doeth God service.”

The council, cut to the heart, took counsel to slay the apostles, thinking they did the will of the Most High. When men believe the law is done away they hold no morals to restrain them, and will put those who teach the truth to death thinking they do the will of God. It is no different from religious leaders today who take counsel against the truth, publish books against it, and would sooner hire accusers than correct themselves.

precepts.text: Paul was brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers.
precepts.point: When men believe the law is done away they hold no morals to restrain them, and will put the teachers to death thinking they do the will of the Most High.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
Who was Gamaliel? Paul says, “I am verily a man which am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, and taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers, and was zealous toward God, as ye all are this day.”

Gamaliel was a Pharisee and a doctor of the law, had in reputation among all the people, and Paul was brought up at his feet in the perfect manner of the law of the fathers. That is the man who stood up in the council and had the apostles put outside a little space.

precepts.text: The God of our fathers raised up Jesus and exalted him to be a Prince and a Saviour, to give repentance to Israel, so the repentance goes to Israel.
precepts.point: When they heard this they held their peace and glorified God, saying the Most High had also to the Gentiles granted repentance unto life. These Gentiles are the Israelites who took on Gentile customs, whether the northern kingdom broken off before Assyria when Pekah the son of Remaliah conspired against Judah, or Judah who became Gentiles under the Greeks.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“When they heard these things, they held their peace, and glorified God, saying, Then hath God also to the Gentiles granted repentance unto life.”

Repentance goes to Israel: “The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree. Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins.”

So the Gentiles granted repentance are Israelites who took on Gentile customs. Either the northern kingdom, broken off before Assyria when Pekah the son of Remaliah conspired against Judah, or Judah who became Gentiles under the Greeks. Christ was exalted to give repentance to Israel, and these Gentiles are Israel.
